status: DRAFT - built from a general understanding of GAF's Certified / Master Elite contractor programs (licensed, insured, reputable, quality-committed, top-tier volume). Not verified against GAF's current program terms. Confirm criteria and weights with GAF / the distributor before relying on scores.
context: GAF is the largest US roofing manufacturer. Its core business is residential steep-slope shingles (Timberline line), with a commercial low-slope line (TPO, modified bitumen). The ideal contractor for GAF is a licensed, insured, reputable roofer who does a steady volume of residential re-roofs and installs GAF systems rather than a competitor's.

criteria.name: Product fit
criteria.measures: How much of the contractor's actual work is what GAF sells: residential steep-slope shingle replacement and repair.

guide.high: Predominantly residential re-roofing / shingle work (reviews and permits describe re-roofs of houses, small multi-family).
guide.mid: Mixed residential and commercial, or residential work that is mostly repairs, or premium materials (slate, tile, metal) alongside shingles.
guide.low: Mostly commercial, flat/low-slope, sheet metal, waterproofing or non-roofing trades.

criteria.name: Project volume
criteria.measures: How many roofing jobs they take on; proxy for how much product they buy.

guide.high: Roughly 20+ distinct roofing-related permit jobs in the last 24 months, or clear evidence of a large, busy operation (a large directory review count, recent reviews, a sizeable crew).
guide.mid: Roughly 5-20 roofing jobs in 24 months, or a healthy review count with no permit data.
guide.low: Little sign of current work: few reviews, none recent, and a very small crew. Permits are a lower bound (most residential re-roofs are never filed), so an empty permit search alone is NOT low volume; recent reviews of completed roofs are direct evidence of current work.

criteria.name: Reputation & workmanship
criteria.measures: What customers say: workmanship, leaks/defects, communication, timeliness, honoring warranties. GAF puts its name on the roof, so callbacks and complaints matter.

guide.high: Consistently positive across many reviews, praise for workmanship, few or no complaints about leaks, warranty or safety.
guide.mid: Generally positive but with recurring complaints (delays, communication) or a small review sample.
guide.low: Multiple complaints about leaks/defects, unhonored warranties, safety or licensing, or a poor average rating.

criteria.name: Licensing & compliance
criteria.measures: Holds the licenses required to operate and appears in good standing.

guide.high: Active required license(s) found and matched, with permits issued under the business's name.
guide.mid: License data unavailable for this jurisdiction or could not be matched, with no red flags (say so; score moderately with low confidence).
guide.low: License expired, suspended, revoked or surrendered; or reviews allege unlicensed work.

criteria.name: Brand alignment
criteria.measures: Evidence that they actually install GAF, and are free to (not locked to a competitor such as CertainTeed or Owens Corning). NOTE: every contractor in this pipeline was found in GAF's own directory, so the listing / certification tier is the shared baseline, not evidence of preference; do not reward it.

guide.high: Reviews or other evidence explicitly name GAF products the contractor installed, and nothing suggests exclusivity with a competitor. (Directory listing alone never reaches this band.)
guide.mid: Only the directory listing, with no brand information either way (score about 55-65), or a genuine mix of several manufacturers.
guide.low: Clearly aligned to a competitor's program (e.g. 'we only install Owens Corning', 'Owens Corning Preferred contractor').

criteria.name: Stability & tenure
criteria.measures: Established business likely to still be around and paying its bills.

guide.high: 10+ years in business, steady activity, evidence spread over several years.
guide.low: Under ~2 years, or activity that just started or stopped.
